verdict.tagline: Launch issues and paid factions weigh heavily on tactical command.
for_you_if: you command historical armies in dedicated multiplayer matches
you master complex tactical positioning and vehicle movement
not_for_you_if: you encounter startup crashes and display launch errors
you expect unpurchased factions to be unlocked immediately
you need stable frame rates on high refresh displays

citations.review_text: let us change our keybinds who tf uses arrow keys

Hi all,

this is single handedly my favorite RTS game to date. Even though CoH3 is out now and I could have bought it as a "newer model" I feel that as a new CoH2 player this game has much more than I could ever need in WW2 RTS gaming. I have no complaints. Aside from small things that may help single player skirmishing.

- Friendly AI OFTEN destroys friendly defenses with vehicles.
- Allowing key binds to be changed
- Allowing the AI to do more with defenses and abilities

(Although I am fairly new so that last could just be a matter of what difficulty I set the bots on)

Aside from those few issues I have had a blast playing this game alone and with friends. The game reminds me of playing a similar game on console when I was a child and I could not remember the name of the game for the life of me. 100% worth it on sale at $12 for all the DLC. Otherwise at full price it's still worth it if you love WW2 and RTS games. On top of that, you can always put it on your wish list and wait for a sale. They go on sale often.

Thanks,
Doc Brown#6832

citations.review_text: Backcapping rat AI plus having less factions in the base game than the original plus dlcs within dlcs plus an egregiously greedy storefront makes a game that could have been great into a test of patience that puts you off from playing at every turn.
abusive uncle game with microtransactions

A brutally unforgiving RTS masterpiece wrapped in a frustratingly greedy monetization scheme.

Company of Heroes 2 remains one of the most intense, strategically demanding, and deeply rewarding real-time strategy games ever created. Unlike traditional base-building games where you can just mass-produce a giant blob of tanks and right-click the enemy base, this game demands absolute, unrelenting tactical focus. The combat is incredibly lethal and dynamic; a single misplaced squad of infantry can be entirely wiped out in a split second by a well-placed artillery shell or a flanking machine gun. It forces you to constantly utilize cover, manage sightlines, and even battle the harsh Russian winter itself. When you successfully execute a coordinated flanking maneuver and watch an enemy heavy tank brew up in flames, the adrenaline rush is unmatched.

However, to experience the full breadth of this incredible tactical sandbox, you have to navigate a monetization system that feels incredibly dated and greedy. While the base game is solid, a massive amount of the game's actual strategic variety—including entire factions, specific commanders, and unique tactical abilities—is locked behind a wall of DLC and microtransactions. It can be deeply frustrating for a new player to load into a multiplayer match and get completely stomped by a highly specific, premium commander ability that they don't have access to unless they open their wallet. It is a brilliant game buried under a very "pay-for-options" business model.

Despite the heavy monetization and its age, the fact that thousands of players are still actively grinding the multiplayer ladders today speaks volumes about the core gameplay loop. For many veteran players, the gritty, heavy, and polished feel of CoH 2 still completely outshines the newer Company of Heroes 3. claims.claim: Vehicles cannot turn in place and require wide turning circles, and anti-tank units manually wheel themselves toward targets before firing rather than rotating instantly.

citations.review_text: Honestly Company of Heroes 1 was great game - a master piece. CoH2 is a poor substitute, honestly half the time your units don't do what you want them to. You can't turn in place, you have to do a large circle now with vehicles - the ai seems to always hit you in the rear. Some maps are great, others are so poorly scripted (as soon you start winning the enemy gets free tanks - you can see it on the graph). I don't know if player vs player the game is more balanced. But the AI in most maps always moves between your lines perfectly (Without being seen) and always knows the best angles to attack cause he can always see your units and there range of fire. This game goes from fun to frustrating in about 60 secs. I find myself baby sitting every single unit in order for it to position itself in cover, or turn to face a enemy (motors seem to turn on their own but anti tank don't its werid - for a unit just to sit still while it gets hammered by a tank - when its whole purpose is to go against tanks.. You think it would turn on its own - or and make sure you manually rotate them, if you click on a anti tank to kill a tank to its right, they wheel themselves to the tank before they fire - its dumb).

Improves upon everything that made Coh1 great but also has divisive choices like commanders...a bit microtransaction heavy...the physics got upgraded,with tanks being able to fall into ice...   


It's a fun game, kinda a unique RTS experience...you manage squads and tanks instead of building a city...need to find cover for your rifleman etcetc... definitely buy, on sale especially... better then Coh3 in my opinion as well...sound design and everything... 


At this point is kinda old so it runs on any system...

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game is heavily monetized through microtransactions and paid commanders, which require grinding or additional purchases.

citations.review_text:
While I still consider CoH1 to be a more revolutionary and iconic experience, CoH2 eventually got gud. There's a lot to love about some of the new mechanics and QoL that was added to this sequel. There's also a lot to hate as well. Microtransactions or grinding for commanders, while something to do, is too tedious for casual players. 

IMHO, this is the best entry in the franchise overall to play currently. An absolute legendary RTS and likely the peak of the IP.

This game is microtransaction heavy. If you were to pay full price for everything this game has to offer, it would cost you over $100. It was not worth that 13 years ago and it isn't worth that much today. Wait for at least a 60% sale for any item you want to buy.

[u]Tutorials[/u]

Tutorials might as well be non-existent.

[u]BASE GAME[/u]

The base game is very small.

The base campaign is pretty fun and not overly difficult and has a compelling story.
You can only play as two factions in multiplayer. The soviets and the Wehrmacht. The game loves to bring up the fact that you can pay another $12 for the US forces, $12 for the OKW, and $12 for the British!!!

[u]THE ARDENNES ASSAULT[/u]

You cannot replay missions at your leisure. If you want to replay a mission you have to restart the campaign.
The US army and OKW are sold separately from the campaign.
This campaign is substantially harder than the base game. You cannot afford to throw away soldiers.
Some missions don't communicate their win conditions properly.
The final mission is tragically easy compared to the rest of the campaign.
The dynamic battles are a nice taste of what multiplayer is like.
Rangers are pay to win. Many missions see you start with a Sherman and a squad of rangers. Rangers also come with Thompson smgs and FREE TOGGLABLE Bazookas!! (For all other infantry taking a support weapon like a bazooka replaces a soldiers primary with that support weapon.

[u]THEATRES OF WAR[/u]

The theatre of war scenarios are pretty good although there are a few that are very poorly balanced. The content for the theatres of war is heavily front loaded in the southern fronts with the other containing 1/2 to 1/4 of the missions of the first.
